why: Bulala held Kanem from the late 14th c. until Idris Katagarmabe's reconquest in the early 16th c.; map flips Bornu/Bulala/nomads every decade
After Katagarmabe's reconquest the Bulala governed Kanem as Bornu vassals until Wadai drove them to Lake Fitri c.1630; map alternates Bornu/Bulala each decade
Bornu general Dala Afuno retook Kanem c.1630 and founded the Dalatoa (Alifa of Mao) line under Bornu; map flips between Bornu, Wadai and the Alifate every decade
In the 19th c. the Dalatoa rulers were Wadai appointees (Kanem a Wadai vassal in 1892, Awlad Sulayman raiding) until the French protectorate of 1899-1900; Rabih's Kanem-Bornu never held Kanem
Baguirmi founded 1522 (capital Massenya); map flips Bornu/Baguirmi each decade
Baguirmi remained a kingdom tributary to Bornu (from Idris Alooma) until independence under Muhammad al-Amin 1751; map shows direct Bornu rule 1620-1760 so Baguirmi vanishes
Baguirmi independent from 1751 until Wadai conquest 1805
Wadai conquered Baguirmi in 1805 and held it tributary until the French protectorate treaty of 1897; map shows Bornu/Saharan nomads in parts in 1890
French protectorate from 1897; colony from 1900-02
Musgum/Massa country between Logone and Chari had no Bornu rule; eastern Musgum only paid tribute to Baguirmi in the 19th c. Map shows Bornu Empire here 1620-1900
The Moundang kingdom of Léré (Gong) lasted until French colonization; map flips Bornu/peoples 1640-1760 and gives Sokoto Caliphate 1820-1900, neither of which ruled Léré
Sara/Kaba country was stateless and raided by Baguirmi, not ruled by Bornu (shown 1640-1830) or Sokoto (shown 1830-1880); incorporated by France early 20th c.
Wadai founded 1635, independent until the French took Abéché in 1909; map flips Wadai/'Saharan nomads' every decade and shows French rule already in 1900
Abéché fell to the French only in 1909 (Ouaddai War 1909-12); map shows French Congo here in 1900
Dar Runga remained a Wadai tributary until the French conquest of Wadai (1909); map shows 'Saharan nomads' 1890 and France 1900
Dar Sila was a Daju sultanate made tributary by Wadai's Sabun (c.1804-15); map shows direct Wadai then 'Saharan nomads' then France 1900
Sultan Muhammad Bakhit's Dar Sila remained independent until the French occupation of 1916
French forces only advanced into Borkou and Ennedi in 1913 (Ain Galaka Nov 1913, Senussi expelled by Feb 1914); map shows France from 1900
Tibesti was first entered by a French column in early 1914; map shows France from 1900
Toubou resistance forced the French out of Tibesti in 1916; reconquered 1929
Rabih installed Muhammad al-Sanusi in Dar al-Kuti in 1890 (capital later N'Délé); map shows unorganized peoples/Rabih then France from 1900
French protectorate treaty 28 Aug 1897; Dar al-Kuti kept its autonomy until al-Sanusi's death in 1911 and the fall of Ouanda Djallé on 17 Dec 1912
Bangassou (Nzakara) sultanate recognized as sovereign in the early 1890s; map shows unorganized peoples in 1890
French protectorate 1894-1917; abolished and put under direct administration only in 1917 (map shows direct French rule from 1900)
Zande sultanate of Zemio (c.1872) independent until French protectorate 12 Apr 1909
French protectorate from 1909; suppressed only in 1923 (map shows direct French rule from 1900)
Old Calabar (Efik) was founded c.1650 in what is now Nigeria; it cannot hold south-west Cameroon from 1400
Mandara (Wandala) kingdom c.1500-1902, capital Dulo from c.1580; map replaces it with direct Bornu rule 1580-1890
Bornu installed Aldawa Nanda in 1614 giving it influence over Mandara, until Mandara defeated Bornu c.1781
Mandara independent after c.1781 (Fulani attacks from 1809) until German conquest in 1902; map shows Bornu then German Kamerun already in 1890
Benue basin (Garoua) had no Bornu rule before the Fulani jihad of 1809; map flips Bornu/peoples every decade
German conquest of Adamawa ran from Jan 1899; Ngaoundéré stormed 20 Aug 1901, Garoua and Rey Bouba taken 1901; map shows German Kamerun already in 1890
Bamum kingdom (Foumban) existed continuously c.1394-1923; map drops it in 1650 for a Bafoussam chiefdom

Portugal only claimed Bioko (Bubi chiefdoms held it; Dutch traded there 1642 without consent) and ceded the claim in 1778; first effective foreign base was British Port Clarence 1827. Map shows Portuguese/Spanish rule and 'Bakweri' (a Cameroonian people) here
After the 1778 cession to Spain the islanders expelled the Spanish and governed themselves; map keeps Portugal here until 1880s
Annobón placed under the Spanish colony of Elobey, Annobón and Corisco from 1843
Part of Spanish Guinea until 1968; map shows Annobón as '(no polity)' from 1890 to 2025
Annobón is part of independent Equatorial Guinea since 1968; map shows '(no polity)'
Spain held only a coastal strip of Río Muni; garrisons were spread through the interior only by 1926 (pacified 1929); map shows Spanish rule from 1890
Príncipe stayed Portuguese until 1975; map shows it as 'Equatorial Guinea [under Spain]' from 1890 and as Equatorial Guinea after 1968
Príncipe Portuguese (as São Tomé)
Príncipe Portuguese until independence 12 July 1975
Independent São Tomé and Príncipe from 12 July 1975; map shows Equatorial Guinea through 2025
Kongo reunified 1709 and continued as a kingdom; map gives these lands to 'Kingdom of Lunda' (1710-1890), which never ruled northern Angola
Kongo became an (intermittent) Portuguese vassal from 1857 and was abolished after the 1914 revolt; map shows Lunda then direct Portuguese rule from 1890
Dembos chiefdoms stayed autonomous until subdued in 1910 (occupation completed 1917); map alternates them with 'Kingdom of Lunda' each decade and shows direct Portuguese rule from 1890
Ndongo (capital Kabasa near N'dalatando) sent embassies to Portugal by 1518 and fought Portugal until 1626; map shows it only 1520-1550 and never in Cuanza Norte
Portuguese-backed Ngola Hari ruled Ndongo from 1626 until the fall of Pungo a Ndongo in 1671
Dutch West India Company held Luanda from 26 Aug 1641 to Aug 1648
'Bakweri' are a Cameroonian people and do not belong in Benguela
São Filipe de Benguela founded 1617; map flips Portuguese/peoples each decade
'Cakaudrove' is a Fijian chiefdom, wrongly placed in southern Angola
Moçâmedes founded by the Portuguese in 1840 with a fort at Ponta Negra
'Cakaudrove' is a Fijian chiefdom, wrongly placed in southern Angola
After the Makololo dynasty fell in 1864 the map restores 'Cakaudrove' (Fijian) here
'Cakaudrove' is a Fijian chiefdom, wrongly placed in southern Angola
Kwanyama kingdom resisted until the Battle of Mongua and fall of N'giva (2 Sep 1915); Ombandja fell in 1907. Map shows direct Portuguese rule from 1890
Bailundo stayed autonomous until the 1902 war (Portuguese columns entered Bailundo 24 Sep 1902)
Kongo's eastern provinces (Nsundi, Mbata) lay here; map gives them to 'Kingdom of Lunda' 1710-1890 alternating with Ngoyo
1885-1908 was Leopold II's personal Congo Free State, not Belgian; Belgium annexed it only on 15 Nov 1908. Map labels it 'Congo, DR (Zaire) [under Belgium]'
Zanzibari/Swahili rule in Maniema ended only with the Congo Arab War (1892-94); map shows Free State rule by 1890
Free State control reached Kivu only after the Congo Arab War (1892-94)
Free State control after defeat of the Zanzibari by early 1894; still Leopold's personal state until 1908
Katanga seceded 11 Jul 1960 until 21 Jan 1963; map shows the secession on only a sliver of the region
South Kasai seceded 9 Aug 1960 (capital Bakwanga) until Oct 1962
Ceded to Germany as Neukamerun by the 4 Nov 1911 Morocco-Congo agreement (districts Wolö-Ntem, Ssanga, Mittel-Ssanga-Lobaye, Ober-Ssanga-Uham); retaken by France in WWI
